_about: THE PIXEL-CENTRE RULE AT THE FRAME'S EDGE, for every picture: planning step 165 of
docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (step 145's recorded deviation 1).
The original draws its frame one sample a pixel, at the pixel's centre, so a quad draws a
pixel when it covers the pixel's CENTRE. The port's engine draws with 4x MSAA, so a picture
whose edge lies in the frame's outer half pixel (a left or top edge at 0.3 px, a right edge
at 1279.69 px) covers the centre of the edge pixel and not all four of its samples: the pixel
blends with what lies behind it where the original's is whole. Step 145 met it on the 44
dark-sky levels and gave their sky a cover (sky.json pixel_cover); this is the rule for every
other picture.
THE REMEDY (sim/EdgeCover; MagicPortalsLayer::syncEdgeCovers). Once a frame, from the
camera and the quads as they are about to be drawn (after the engine's interpolation and the
earthquake's shake), every visible axis-aligned quad whose edge lies in the band gets a STRIP:
a second quad of the same material over the gap between its edge and the frame's pixel
boundary, along the picture's own rows or columns, its uv the picture's own linear map
carried on across it. The picture's quad is untouched and the strip never overlaps it, so a
translucent picture is blended once and no pixel but an edge pixel can change.
THE COMPLEMENT (the key below): the same rule at a picture's INWARD edge in the outer pixel - the
black bars a tremble moves past the top or the bottom - a strip over the rest of the pixel where the
centre is covered, and the quad left out of the frame for that frame where it covers samples and no
centre (EdgeCover::Snap, Culled).
WHAT IT LEAVES: a picture's edge inside the frame, and an edge that does not cover the edge
pixel's centre (past the band), stay the MSAA blends they were; so does a turned quad, a quad
with a sheet's rotated uv, a picture that goes on inward from an edge in the pixel's inner half (the
log says 'edge sliver'), and a sky that already has its cover (sky.json pixel_cover).
THE FRAME is 1280 x 720 unless a ViewportInfo says otherwise, and the game never sets one (only the
editor does), so the rule always runs against 1280 x 720 pixels, as the sky's cover does. In a window of
another size the band, the first sample and the cull's 'outer pixel' are 1280-pixel units, not the window's:
a strip still lands (2-05 at 1920 x 1080: columns 1918 and 1919 equal), a bar's edge 0.6 real pixels in
would be culled though it covers its pixel's centre, and no original frame exists at another size.

_enabled: true is THE ORIGINAL'S FRAME: a picture whose edge lies in the frame's outer half pixel is
drawn out to the frame's pixel boundary, by the strip above. false draws the pictures alone,
as the port did before step 165.
The original's frame is one sample a pixel at the pixel's centre: its library frames are flat
at both edges where the art is (step 145's evidence, out/parity/program/EC/), and its
surface comes from ConfigChooser, which asks EGL for no EGL_SAMPLES and takes the first exact
asantee/gs2d/ConfigChooser.java:24-25 and 48-66; GL2JNIView.java:121). That the first such
config is single-sampled is INFERRED from EGL 1.4's sort (section 3.4.1.2: fewer sample
buffers, then fewer samples, first), not read on the emulator. The engine draws with 4x MSAA
_band_px: The distance of an edge pixel's CENTRE from the frame's side: half a pixel. A low edge at or
before it, or a high edge past it, draws that pixel under the pixel-centre rule
(Sky::PixelCover's ceil(e - 0.5)). Decoded from the rule, not measured.
_first_sample_px: The first sample of the 4x pattern from a pixel's side: Vulkan's standard 4-sample positions
0.125, 0.375, 0.625 and 0.875 along each axis. A picture edge nearer the frame's side than
this leaves every sample of the edge pixel covered, so no strip is asked for. The specification's
own positions, not a measurement of this machine's device.
_turn_rad: A quad turned by more than this about any axis is not an axis-aligned picture, so its edges
are not the frame's rows and columns and it keeps the MSAA blend (the port's own choice: a
turned sprite's pixel-centre coverage is not a strip's).
_guess: the tolerance only. The port's own number, neither decoded nor measured: a quad turned by no more than
_complement: THE COMPLEMENTARY HALF of the rule: the pictures whose INWARD edge lies in the frame's outer pixel,
which the strips above (the edge that faces the frame's own side) leave as MSAA blends. The black
bars (z 1.0, art.json black_bar) are the case the program met: the earthquake moves the camera past
the scene's top or bottom and their inward edge crosses the first or last row by fractions of a pixel.
Under the pixel-centre rule the row is the bar's whole where the edge is past its centre and the
scene's whole where it is not; the 4x pattern gave a half or three quarters of the bar's black between.
true: (1) a picture that begins outside the frame and covers the outer pixel's centre gets a strip
over the rest of the pixel, its inward edge in (band_px, 1 - first_sample_px] from the side, the same
strip as above; (2) a picture whose part on the frame lies wholly in one outer pixel and covers its
centre nowhere is left out of the frame for that frame (its quad hidden, restored before the next
frame's first line of game code). false: the first half alone, as the first build of step 165 drew.
What neither does: a picture that goes on inward from an edge in the pixel's inner half (its edge
0.5 to 0.875 px in, the picture beyond) keeps its MSAA samples of that pixel - a strip adds samples,
a cull takes a whole quad - and the layer says so in the log (edge sliver). Decoded from the same rule
_log_every_frame: A measuring switch, false as shipped. The log says each strip, cull and kept edge once, the frame it first
appears, 64 a level at most; true says every one of them every frame with no cap, so a capture of a pan or a
tremble (--screenshot-every 1, one frame a tick under --fixed-step) carries the rule's own answer for each
frame - which picture's edge lay where in the outer pixel - to set the frame's edge pixels against. Nothing is
drawn differently. The port's own, not the original's.
_pool_size: The strips made ready when the layer attaches, hidden, before it makes any other entity
(MagicPortalsLayer::buildEdgeCoverPool). The port's own number, not the original's: a strip is an
entity, and the renderer breaks a tie between draws of one depth and key by the order the registry
stores them in. An entity made in the middle of a run and later left standing at the end of a store
moves another entity when something earlier is destroyed, so strips made on demand reordered the
additive particles of one system and moved a pixel of their glow by one 5/6/5 step (the first
sweep of step 165: 133 px outside the outer ring on 2-16, 3-21, 3-23, 4-19 and 4-28). Made
first, they are never the last of a store and move nothing. 24 is above the most any level's rest
frame needs (one, 2-05's wall) and above what a pan asks; a level that asks for more makes the
rest on demand, the late way, and says nothing.
A hidden strip is not gathered, but it is still an entity with a material: it keeps the texture
paths of the last picture it copied, and a lightmapped picture's are a lightmap the level's unload
invalidates, which the renderer would load again for the strip (the level walk's 259 failures, step
165's verification). So the layer clears every strip's texture paths when a level unloads, and
keeps the entities where they are.
_guess: the size only. 0 makes none ready.
